```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 7
    n_vehicles = 3
    Q = 50  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[12, 16], [46, 89], [73, 39], [64, 26], [12, 77], [46, 90], [63, 21]]
    demands = [14, 8, 10, 25, 16, 7, 19]
    time_windows = [[0, 326], [60, 111], [47, 110], [47, 129], [46, 125], [66, 165], [64, 132], [54, 145]]
    service_times = [9, 11, 7, 10, 8, 6, 8]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Distribution Planning Team
From: Logistics Operations Manager
Subject: Vehicle Routing and Scheduling Challenge with Customer Time Windows

Overview
We are planning a delivery cycle using a small fleet of identical vehicles operating from a single central depot. The task is to route the fleet so that every customer is served exactly once within their promised delivery time windows. All vehicles will depart the depot at time 0 and must return and check in before the depot’s latest allowable return time.

Challenge Description
Each vehicle will perform one out-and-back trip: leave the depot at time 0, visit an assigned sequence of customers, and return to the depot before closing time. The core challenge is to assign customers to vehicles and determine visit sequences so that we honor all time windows, meet service durations at each stop, and keep each vehicle’s load within capacity while controlling total cost. If a vehicle arrives at a customer before the earliest acceptable time, it will wait on site and begin unloading when the window opens; late starts are not allowed. After service at a stop is completed, the vehicle immediately departs for the next location.

Operating Rules and Constraints
- Fleet usage and cost: Vehicles are identical. Activating a vehicle for the day incurs a fixed deployment cost, in addition to distance-based travel cost. We aim to balance the number of vehicles used with route distances.
- Departure and return: All vehicles depart at time 0. Each route must return to the depot on or before the depot’s latest return time. Each vehicle makes a single continuous trip.
- Travel time: Travel time between any two locations is equal to the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with an implicit speed of 1 so that one unit of distance equals one unit of time.
- Time windows: Each customer has an earliest and latest start time for service. Service must start within this window. Early arrivals wait until the window opens; waiting counts against the available time before the next commitments.
- Service times: Each customer requires a defined unloading/service duration. Departure from a stop occurs at the actual start of service plus this service time.
- Capacity: Each customer has a delivery quantity. The sum of quantities carried on any route cannot exceed the vehicle’s capacity at any point during the trip.
- Coverage: Every customer must be visited exactly once. No split deliveries are allowed.

Goal
Develop a set of routes that visits every customer exactly once, respects customer time windows, service durations, capacity limits, and the depot closing time, while minimizing total cost. Total cost consists of the sum of travel distances across all vehicles plus the fixed deployment costs for the vehicles we choose to use.

Expected Planning Outputs
- Routes for each deployed vehicle showing customer visit order and planned arrival and departure times at each stop and at the depot.
- Verification that all time windows, service durations, capacity limits, and the depot closing time are satisfied.
- A summary of total distance traveled, number of vehicles deployed, and the resulting total cost.

ANNEX – Operations Data
- Depot location (coordinates): (50, 50)
- Depot latest return time: 326
- Customer locations (coordinates): Customer Locations (coordinates):

  - C2: (46, 89)

  - C6: (46, 90)
  - C7: (63, 21)
- Customer delivery quantities: Customer Demands:
  - C1: 14 units
  - C2: 8 units
  - C3: 10 units
  - C4: 25 units
  - C5: 16 units
  - C6: 7 units
  - C7: 19 units
- Customer time windows (earliest, latest): Customer Time Windows [earliest, latest]:
  - C1: [60, 111]
  - C2: [47, 110]
  - C3: [47, 129]
  - C4: [46, 125]
  - C5: [66, 165]
  - C6: [64, 132]
  - C7: [54, 145]
- Service/unloading times at customers: Service Times (minutes at customer):
  - C1: 9
  - C2: 11

  - C4: 10
